sections.title: General Information
paragraphs: Nassau Life Insurance Company of Kansas
For Approval Purposes
We are filing the above-referenced forms for approval. The forms are filed in accordance with the Uniform Standards and are
laser printed, subject only to minor variations in paper stock, color, fonts, duplexing, positioning, and pagination. These forms
are new and are not intended to replace existing forms.
Contract forms 26FIA and 26FIAN are Single Premium Individual Deferred Fixed Indexed Annuity base contracts designed to
provide a series of periodic payments based on the Annuitization Value on the Contract Maturity Date and the performance of
various selected accounts. These contracts include a return of premium surrender charge and death benefit. These two base
contracts are substantially similar except 26FIA includes a premium bonus feature and 26FIAN does not. When 26FIA is
issued, the Premium Bonus is applied to the Account Value on the date the premium is applied to the contract. The amount of
the Premium Bonus will be based on the amount of the premium payment and the applicable Premium Bonus Percentage
shown on the schedule pages. With both contracts, at the time of issue, the initial premium (and any applicable Premium
Bonus) will be applied to the contract and allocated in accordance with the premium allocation chosen at the time of
application, subject to a Minimum Allocation Percentage and a Minimum Allocation Amount. Both contracts provide fixed and
indexed account options to which the client can allocate their premium and Premium Bonus, if applicable. The fixed account
will accumulate at a specified interest rate, while any chosen indexed account’s growth will be based on the performance of
those particular indexes over a period of time, subject to the terms of any applicable indexed account strategy rider(s) attached
to the contract. A negative Index Credit will never be applied to the contract.
Forms 26FIASP and 26FIASPN are contract schedule pages and will be issued with a base contract (26FIASP will be issued
with 26FIA and 26FIASPN will be issued with 26FIAN). In addition to ordinary case-specific information, the schedule pages
will include information regarding the various indexed accounts that are available with the product. These forms are
substantially similar except form 26FIASP includes information related to the premium bonus feature of the contract and form
26FIASPN does not.
Form 26MVA is a market value adjustment amendment. There is no charge for this amendment and it is not an option selected
at the time of application. The company may decide to offer or cease offering this feature for new issues at any time.
Form 26PTPHS is a rider form, specific to the indexed account feature of the base contract, which may be used with this
product. The form describes a particular indexed account crediting methodology and will be issued with the contract if an
indexed account with the particular crediting methodology is offered at the time of issue.
Forms 26NHWP and 26TIW2P are nursing home and terminal illness waiver amendments which, if included with the issued
contract, will provide a waiver of certain charges if the Owner meets specified criteria. There is no charge for these
amendments and they are not an option selected at the time of application. The company may decide to offer or cease offering
any of these amendments for new issues at any time.
Forms 26GLWB and 26GLWB2 are guaranteed lifetime withdrawal benefit riders that provide guaranteed withdrawals up to the
Annual Benefit Amount each Rider Year following the Rider Exercise Date for the life of the Covered Person(s) regardless of
the value of the base contract. These rider forms are substantially similar, with the main difference being that 26GLWB
includes an Early Income Benefit Base Bonus feature, whereas 26GLWB2 does not include this feature. There is a charge for
these riders.
Form 26EWB is a guaranteed withdrawal benefit riders including a Care Benefit Base feature, that provide guaranteed
withdrawals up to the Enhanced Benefit Amount following the Rider Exercise Date as long as the Covered Person(s) meets
certain qualifying conditions, regardless of the value of the base contract. This rider is issued in conjunction with a guaranteed
lifetime withdrawal benefit rider as part of the same contract. The Enhanced Withdrawal Benefit rider is NOT intended to be
qualified for long-term care as defined in the Internal Revenue Code or by the National Association of Insurance
Commissioners and does not qualify for any preferred tax treatment.
Form 26GMDB, is a guaranteed minimum death benefit rider that provides a death benefit which may exceed that provided by
the base annuity contract.
Form 26RSP is a specification page that act as a cover page for the guaranteed withdrawal and guaranteed death benefit
riders we may offer with our suite of Fixed Indexed Annuity contracts and describes rider terms (“Rider Specifications”) which
apply to all of those elected riders (e.g., Rider Fee, Roll-up Period, Roll-up Restart, etc.). The riders that have been elected at
the time of application and issued with the contract will appear in the “Rider Components” field. Any reference in the riders to
“Rider Components” is referring to the forms listed in this “Rider Components” field. Please refer to this field for the list of riders
that each specification page may be used with.
At the time of product launch, we intend to use the above forms with the following previously approved forms:
Forms OL5630 and OL5631 - Premium Allocation and Rider Election Form (Approval: 12/6/2024, SERFF Tracking no. UNAM-
Form OL5629 – Application for Individual Fixed Indexed Annuity (Approval: 12/6/2024, SERFF Tracking no. UNAM-
**Please note, this company is in the process of changing its name from Nassau Life Insurance Company of Kansas to Nassau
Insurance Company of Texas. The name has been pre-approved by the Texas Department of Insurance. This pre-approval
has been included in the Supporting Documentation tab for your records. We will be submitting formal name change
applications in each of the individual states. We have filed these forms with the new company name in anticipation of these
filings and will not issue the forms until the name change is final.
This submission, including charges and other values, is for specimen purposes only. Other scenarios may generate additional
text information in the specifications and tables sections of the forms. An actuarial memorandum is enclosed for these forms.
These forms may also be used with previously and subsequently approved contracts. Text ordinarily bracketed appears in the
forms and is described on the attached Statement of Variability. Any requisite fees and filing documents have been included
with this filing.
Your attention to this submission is appreciated. Should you have any questions regarding any of the materials in this filing,
please do not hesitate to contact me at (860) 403-3278 or by e-mail at sdaley@nfg.com.
Thank you,
Shanique Daley
Product Analyst

sections.title: Objection Letter
paragraphs: Dear Shanique Daley,
Please respond to the following objection(s).
Objection 1
The Department’s procedure as clarified in AID Declaratory Order No. 2016-091 shall apply from the effective date of Bulletin
14-2016, November 9, 2016, and until or unless replaced or superseded by a Rule or change in law.  The rate and form review time
period that the Insurance Commissioner has to affirmatively approve or disapprove the form or rate under Ark. Code Ann. Sec.
23-79-109(b)(1) begins when the rate or form is filed with the Department.  The Commissioner may extend that time period by not
more than an additional thirty (30) days by giving notice of the extension before expiration of the initial thirty (30) day period pursuant
to Ark. Code Ann. Sec. 23-79-109(b)(3).  The initial time frame will no longer be tolled due to unresolved deficiencies or outstanding
objections, inquiries, or request for information to the insurer.  The Department will communicate any deficiencies in the filing to the
insurer and attempt to resolve prior to the expiration of the time period; however, outstanding deficiencies may result in filings being
affirmatively disapproved in order to guard against deficient filings being approved by operation of law.  If disapproved, an insurer
may submit, within any applicable deadlines, a new filing for the Department's consideration.
Please feel free to contact me if you have questions.
Sincerely,
John Jeanes
